GomeBoy 1.4.0 fixes deterministic session recording and replay for network link-cable sessions.

## Link-cable recording and replay

Session recordings previously captured joypad transitions but not the bits and clock timing supplied by a network link peer. Linked sessions such as Pokémon Red Cable Club trades could therefore replay correctly up to the trade, then diverge and fail final cycle verification. That also prevented `gomeboy-stream` from reliably rendering those recordings to video.

Network link activity is now captured as part of the recording:

- the frame and cycle where the link is attached;
- incoming bits from internally-clocked exchanges;
- external clock pulses at the cycle they become ready.

Replay starts unplugged, re-attaches the recorded peer at the original point, and only returns link results at their recorded cycles. Timing drift now fails at the exact link event instead of silently replaying a different session.

Recordings that never use a link remain unchanged on disk because the new `links` manifest field is omitted when empty.

Regression coverage includes internal- and external-clock transfers with non-deterministic peer timing and verifies that a linked recording replays without the original peer.

## Development since v1.3.1

This release also contains the GBA implementation groundwork merged since v1.3.1, including CPU, PPU, DMA, timers, interrupts, keypad, Direct Sound, save hardware, scheduler/power work, and the deterministic conformance runner.

## What's Changed

* fix(recording): record network link results so linked sessions replay in https://github.com/maestroi/gomeboy/pull/98
